claims.text: The lightweight HEA's combination of low density, mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance arises from a single-phase, high-entropy-stabilized solid solution.
A high-entropy-stabilized solid solution suppresses the formation of brittle intermetallics.
The single-phase structure enables a uniform distribution of alloying elements.
Uniformly distributed alloying elements confer mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid solution.
Entropy stabilization prevents elemental segregation and intermetallic formation.
The absence of brittle phases maintains mechanical integrity.
Distributing corrosion- and oxidation-resistant elements throughout the matrix enhances environmental durability.
The lightweight HEA will have lower density than the lower-configurational-entropy baseline alloy.
The lightweight HEA will have higher yield strength and ductility than the baseline alloy.
The lightweight HEA will show lower corrosion mass loss or higher polarization resistance than the baseline alloy.
The lightweight HEA will show a lower oxide-scale growth rate and lower oxidation mass gain than the baseline alloy.
The hypothesis should cease to hold if the HEA forms multiple phases or intermetallics because of insufficient entropy or unfavorable element selection.
At sufficiently high temperatures, enthalpy-driven phase separation can overcome entropy stabilization.
Failure to outperform the baseline in at least two of three property categories would falsify the hypothesis.
Significant intermetallic or multiphase formation would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Multiphase or intermetallic formation is defined both as a condition outside the hypothesis's stated domain and as a result that falsifies the hypothesis. A boundary-condition violation does not by itself test the mechanism within its claimed domain.

The prediction claims superiority in all listed property categories, but the falsification rule permits failure in one of the three tested performance categories without falsification and does not include the predicted density advantage.
